name: Sengele
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Guthrie, Malcolm. 1948. The Classification of the Bantu Languages. London: International African Institute / Oxford University Press, pp. 36-39 (Zone C, 'Characteristics common to Zone C', item 10); read only in the French translation by Labaere, H. R. 2001. 'Guthrie et la Zone C. Traduction et commentaire du point de vue tɛtɛla C71'. Annales Aequatoria 22: 163-183. Sengele-specific description checked and silent: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2001. 'Notes sur le parler Sɛ́ŋgɛlɛ de Mbɛ́lɔ (Maindombe - R.D. Congo)'. Annales Aequatoria 22: 259-326 (DOI 10.4314/aq.v22i1.5596).
catalog_locator: Labaere 2001, p. 172, section 'I. Caractéristiques communes à la Zone C', item 10, translating Guthrie 1948: 36-39; zone framing on pp. 164-165. Motingea 2001: sec. 2.4 'Tons' pp. 280-284 and 2.5 'Syllabe' p. 284.
catalog_quote: Quoique cette Zone couvre une superficie très étendue, et comprend huit groupes qui contiennent environ quarante langues, ces langues attestent pourtant une remarquable relation d'affinité. ... I. Caractéristiques communes à la Zone C. ... 9. Une seule more (quantité) seulement sur la voyelle de radicaux. (De même dans les Zones A,B,D.) ... 10. Accent d'intensité sur la syllabe du radical (Ainsi en Zone B.) 11. Ton lexical tant sur le radical que sur les suffixes. (Ainsi en Zones B,D,L)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for Sengele, so there is nothing to agree or disagree with; this is the first stress statement held by the project, but it is (a) second-hand, via Labaere's French translation, and (b) a zone-level generalisation over ~40 Zone C languages, not an observation about Sengele. The archive.org item classificationof0000guth (1967 reprint) is lending-only: access-restricted-item=true, and pdf marked private, both download attempts could not be reached by automated download. HathiTrust catalog search could not be reached by automated download bot-block page.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zone-wide feature: a stress (intensity) accent falls on the radical (root/stem-initial) syllable of the word; stated for all of Guthrie's Zone C ('eight groups containing about forty languages', p. 164 of Labaere's translation) and also for Zone B. Not a Sengele-specific statement; Sengele is C33 in Guthrie's referential classification (Motingea 2001: 259).
new_statements.exceptions: none stated; Labaere adds commentary to neighbouring items 9, 12 and 13 but none to item 10
new_statements.identity_note: Guthrie's statement is about Zone C as a whole (and Zone B), not about Sengele in particular; Sengele's group number in the 1948 scheme could not be checked (Labaere's translation cites Bobangi as 21b, Ntomba as 25, Ngombe as 31, i.e. the 1948 numbering differs from the later C33). The quote is Labaere's French rendering; Guthrie's English wording was not seen. Labaere's own commentary concerns Tetela (C71).

new_statements.quote: 9. Une seule more (quantité) seulement sur la voyelle de radicaux. (De même dans les Zones A,B,D.) ... 10. Accent d'intensité sur la syllabe du radical (Ainsi en Zone B.) 11. Ton lexical tant sur le radical que sur les suffixes. (Ainsi en Zones B,D,L)
new_statements.translation: 9. Only a single mora (quantity) on the vowel of radicals. (Likewise in Zones A, B, D.) ... 10. Stress (intensity accent) on the radical syllable (thus also in Zone B). 11. Lexical tone on the radical as well as on the suffixes. (Thus in Zones B, D, L)

new_statements.relation_note: Identical source: the catalog record (classification morphological) and the one existing statement both rest on this same passage in the same held translation; 167 / printed p. 172). No independent confirmation is added and Guthrie's English wording is still unseen. The first-hand Sengele descriptions held (Motingea 2001; Ilonga 1991) remain silent on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zone-level generalisation for Guthrie's Zone C (c. 40 languages in 8 groups; Sengele = C33 per Motingea 2001): word stress falls on the radical (root) syllable, alongside lexical tone on radical and suffixes. Second-hand (via translation) and not a Sengele-specific observation; Labaere adds no commentary to item 10.
new_statements.identity_note: Guthrie's statement concerns Zone C as a whole (8 groups, c. 40 languages) and does not name Sengele; Sengele is placed at C33 by Motingea 2001 (variety of Mbɛ́lɔ). Labaere's translation and commentary are written from the Tetela (C71) point of view.

sources.note: Silent on stress. Sec. 2 'Sons' pp. 263-284 covers vowels (elision, contraction, harmony), semi-vowels, consonants, 2.4 'Tons' pp. 280-284 (two categories: simple tones L and H, complex double rising/falling and triple tones; 'Comme ailleurs en bantou, les tons en k[ɛ]mb[ɛ́]l[ɔ] ont une double valeur: lexicale et grammaticale' p. 281; fusion, harmony, contrast, lowering rules) and 2.5 'Syllabe' p. 284 (open syllables V, CV, CSV, syllabic nasal). The word 'accent' occurs only as 'accent aigu' = H-tone mark (p. 280). No accent d'intensité / stress / penultimate-lengthening remark anywhere in pp…

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2010. Aspects des parlers minoritaires des lacs Tumba et Inongo. ILCAA Language Monograph Series 5. Tokyo: ILCAA. Conclusions, sec. 4 'Baséngele', pp. 227-228.
sources.note: Sengele is not treated in the volume but summarised from Motingea 2001: classification remarks (not Mongo, not Kongo/Teke; C33 bangi-ntomba group), a list of sound correspondences (*p > p/w, *me- > mi-, *N-V > nd, lateral weakening, regressive and progressive vowel harmony) and morphology. Nothing on accent or stress.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2009. Le réseau fluvial.. (Annales Aequatoria 30: 839-988) -- an earlier compilation 'source named' (Motingea 2009, 'pp. 27-28').
sources.note: Mentions the Basɛ́ngɛlɛ only ethnohistorically (as Badya/Lia conquerors around the equatorial lakes) and cites Ilonga 1994; no Sengele phonology, no accent statement. The scan's 'pp. 27-28' pointer could not be matched to any Sengele description.

Useful only as tone-marked data, not as a description.
